Title: Example row - the shape of an owner decision brief
OneLine: the one-line form status.md projects - what is being decided, and the recommendation in a clause
Decision: What is being decided, who raised it and when, and any context a ruler needs that is not obvious from the one-line.
BlastRadius: What breaks or changes if this is ruled either way - the honest cost, not the optimistic one.

Title: Retire open-items.md for one generated HTML reference view
OneLine: rule whether open-items.md is retired outright for a single generated HTML owner surface - ruled (b): open-items.csv is the source, open-items.html is the view
Decision: Raised at the first re-attestation sitting: the generated pending projection was a POINTER where the owner needed the before/after, and the depth that makes a re-attest readable is a word-level diff, which markdown cannot express. The owner went further than the format question: -open-items.md is no longer even necessary; a single html reference view is sufficient, the md can be retired in its entirety.-
BlastRadius: Kit-wide, not local: OPEN_ITEMS.template.md is a bootstrap MAPPING destination (every adopting repo has one), 11 kit-doc references, 7 test modules, one SR/LLR/TC row, and agent_dispatch uses the file as a status-map marker while refreshing its pending block every dispatch loop. A kit version bump with a documented migration.
Options: (a) HTML view over per-item markdown sources - prose stays writable and diffable, but keeps a directory of prose files as a second authoring surface · (b) HTML view over a CSV registry - one registry, one view; OI state becomes queryable; prose authors into cells · (c) fold OI state into work-items.csv - blurs decision-vs-work · (d) keep the file and add HTML depth beside it - leaves two surfaces where the owner wants one.
Recommendation: Driver recommended (a); owner ruled (b), on the framing that settles the prose-in-cells objection: the briefs are pulled into the generator to construct the HTML, which is what a human actually references, so the CSV is a machine source read raw exactly as often as work-items.csv is - never.

Title: concurrency-v2 B2: strike or restate the specs-mirror-the-terminal-folders sentence
OneLine: rule whether concurrency-v2 B2's second sentence is STRUCK or RESTATED after WI-391 measured it and handed the row back - recommendation: restate
Decision: B2 says a closed WI's spec-of-record moves to docs/archive/specs/complete/ or docs/archive/specs/cancelled/ rather than one flat docs/archive/specs/, so a spec's location answers shipped-or-cancelled without opening it. WI-391 was filed to build it and instead REFUTED it on measurement; an independent review confirmed the refutation (APPROVE findings=6, commit 2a4c9642). The evidence: (1) the mapping from spec to terminal folder is NOT TOTAL - of 111 archived specs, 92 resolve to complete and 3 to cancelled, while 16 have no derivable terminal state (15 shared effort docs, which docs/specs/README.md makes a first-class shape, plus WI-300-sr052-binding.2026-07-26.md, whose name does not match _own_spec's own WI-###.<date>.md glob); (2) it is CONTRADICTORY for at least one file - research-knowledge.2026-07-29.md is cited by WI-138/WI-145 (complete) and WI-158 (cancelled), and R-F archives a shared doc when its LAST open citer closes, so both answers are correct; (3) there is NO REGENERATOR to hang a freshness gate off - gen_trajectory.py contains the string 'archive' zero times - so the folder would be hand-maintained derived data, the one shape this kit's generated-not-hand-maintained rule forbids; (4) for the 92 attributable specs the answer ALREADY EXISTS BY LOCATION one directory over, in the docs/work/complete/ vs docs/work/cancelled/ split WI-384 built, so the mirror answers 'shipped' 97% of the time for a question one ls already answers; (5) no tool consumes the split - check_trajectory's ARCHIVE_SPECS_DIR (:161), _own_spec (:1775) and its glob (:1796), and tests/test_trajectory_specs.py:511 would all have to WIDEN to recurse, i.e. the required code change is to ignore the distinction (docs/orphans-allow:50 survives only because fnmatch '*' spans separators). Cost is NOT the objection and was measured to remove that defence: the one-time migration was prototyped as a dry run at about 70 lines. Its real size is larger than the intake stated - 124 inbound link targets across 25 files resolved by path (not the 101 literal-string matches), plus 91 outbound links across 43 of the 111 files that a one-level-deeper move rebases, the WI-353 defect - about 215 targets, 92 of them in the append-compiled docs/log.md.
BlastRadius: Small and fully enumerated, either way: one sentence in docs/concurrency-v2.md B2; one queued row (WI-391, parked queued+blockref on this item); and two docs/declared-absences entries whose reasons now point here. Those two lines must be RESTATED, never deleted - deleting them adds +2 dangling references to check_doc_refs --strict, because the WI-391 spec's own title text names both paths at line 3 and survives any disposition (measured). Nothing in docs/archive/specs/ moves under either option, so no link migration is incurred and no downstream repo is affected.
Options: (a) RESTATE - amend B2's second sentence to record that the goal is met by the registry half for every attributable spec and is unmeetable by any folder layout for the 16 that are not. FOR: keeps the owner's ruling and its reasoning in the record, states WHY the flat home is correct so the next reader does not re-file it, and costs one sentence. AGAINST: leaves a sentence that reads as a partial retreat rather than a clean decision. (b) STRIKE - delete the sentence outright. FOR: shortest text, no lingering half-rule. AGAINST: deletes an owner ruling with no record of why, so the same row gets re-filed the next time someone reads a flat docs/archive/specs/ and reaches for the obvious tidy-up - which is exactly how WI-391 came to exist. (c) BUILD IT ANYWAY - accept a hand-adjudicated placement for the 16. FOR: B2 ships as written. AGAINST: asserts a terminal state the repo does not hold for 14% of the corpus, creates a second uncross-checked home for a fact the registry already carries, and adds a decision with a wrong-answer mode to every future close.
Recommendation: RESTATE, do not strike - the driver's recommendation, the reviewer's, and the coordinator's. The GOAL in B2 is sound and is already achieved: a spec's shipped-or-cancelled IS answerable by location, just at docs/work/ rather than at docs/archive/specs/, which is the registry half WI-384 built. The sentence is wrong only in WHERE it puts the answer. Striking it would delete an owner ruling and leave no record of the measurement that refuted it, and the 16 undecidable files are the durable reason a future reader needs - they do not go away, so without the restated sentence the tidy-up gets re-proposed. Restating also gives the two declared-absences entries an honest referent.
